Q: How to get the numeric value that does not end with `%` A:

You can use the following pattern to match the strings you're looking for:

\b\d+\.\d+(?! ?%)\b

Demonstration: https://regex101.com/r/LiIojB/1

Explanation:

  • \b matches a word boundary, which is a location in a string between an alphanumerical character and a whitespace or punctuation character. I put one at the beginning and end of the pattern to prevent it from matching more than what you're looking for.

  • \d matches a digit character, shorthand for [0-9]. You can use [0-9] instead if you find it more intuitive or your regex engine doesn't recognize \d.

  • I assume you understand the + operator and the literal ..

  • (?! ...) defines a negative lookahead group. In this case, it contains the pattern ?%, which is an optional space followed by a percentage sign. So if the current match isn't followed by a percentage sign, or a space and then a percentage sign, the match will fail.

Q: How to publish a website with HTML generated by AI (no terminal, no Git)? A:

If you are using agentic AI and/or a harness like Claude Code then the agent could be tasked with setting up suitable a hosting environment for the site, and then deploying the generated code to it automatically (or on request from you).

If not, you'll need to do that task yourself manually. If you're simply using an AI chatbot and getting the HTML back in the conversation then ultimately it's a copy-and-paste job to put the HTML into a file and upload it to whatever hosting environment you decide is suitable. Once such an environment is set up it should be the work of a few moments to save and upload a file.
